title: Theodore of Mopsuestia, Twenty-Five Books Against Eunomius
english: I read the twenty-five books of Theodore of Antioch against Eunomius in defense of St. Basil. His style is somewhat obscure, but the work is full of ideas and sound reasoning, and contains a wealth of evidence taken from the Scriptures. He refutes the arguments of Eunomius almost word for word, and amply proves that he is very ignorant of outside knowledge and still more so of our religion. I believe he is the Theodore who was bishop of Mopsuestia.
translator_notes: Greek locked from Bekker 1824; Freese 1920 used as PD English reference only.
Codex 4 of 279; Theodore of Mopsuestia (c. 350–428), bishop 394, greatest exegete of Antiochene school. Works mostly lost; this 25-book treatise against Arianism is a major loss.
Eunomius (d. 393), bishop of Cyzicus, Arian. Basil the Great (330–379) defended orthodoxy.
